items.title: Mike Longo interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 13, 2019
items.q: Count Basie swung but that ain’t the same swing that Dizzy played with.

ctx.x: Yeah. Dizzy’s music, say Count Basie swung but that ain’t the same swing that Dizzy played with. If you think about Freddie Green going ching-ching-ching, you can’t do that to a tune [scats]. See how do you do that? And so what Dizzy and them did was found a new way to swing. A new kind of beat and all that. But that’s how jazz has evolved over the time. And so Dizzy took issue with a guy in England that was interviewing him that was talking about the bebop revolution. He said it wasn’t a revolution it was an…

This is great. A little while ago you used the word “comping.” I wanted to ask you about comping behind Joe Williams and Nancy Wilson and Jimmy Witherspoon. How does a piano player learn to be an accompanist that vocalists want to work with?
